newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 10.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, July 10.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue chip share index ended with modest gains as the market breathed a collective sigh of relief that the Bank of England raised official interest rates by only 25 basis points, dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,767.8, up 5.4 points, or 0.11 percent.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index tumbled about 1.6 percent in active bourse dealings, hurt by the dollar falling more than a pfennig on comments from the Bundesbank that the U.S. currency's correction was now over. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,992.38, down 63.48 points, or 1.57 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,000.65, down 26.32 points, or 0.65 percent.

PARIS - Shares closed lower but ended above their lows as a higher start on Wall Street helped pull shares back up somewhat, dealers said. A 1.51 percent overnight fall on Wednesday, coupled with an easier dollar and a weaker franc, hurt share prices and prompted investors to take profits. The CAC-40 index closed down 21.47, or 0.73 percent, at 2,929.09.

ZURICH - Shares ended sharply lower but dealers said the consolidation after a series of record-hitting sessions was welcome rather than disturbing. The Swiss market index closed at 5,885.4, down 91.7 points, or 1.53 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed mostly lower as the bourse paused for breath and investors took some profits after the leaps and bounds of recent days. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,828, down 67 points, or 0.48 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares tumbled, undermined at the opening by a weak Wall Street close, which prompted a bout of profit-taking on a blue-chip AEX index which has recently raced to consecutive record highs. The AEX index closed at 924.71, down 10.66 points, or 1.14 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed modestly higher, as high technology shares were bought following a record winning streak in technology stocks on Wall Street, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,754.78, up 57.61 points, or 0.29 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks finished sharply higher after a rally in the lagging property sector and a rebound in red chip shares allowed prices to shrug off early losses. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,839.23, up 135.50 points, or 0.92 percent.

SYDNEY - The share market almost wiped out all of its earlier losses as bank stocks rebounded when long bond yields fell on hopes of a further rate cut following a weak set of June jobs data. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,694.4, down 1.7 points, or 0.06 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares basked in the warmth of a much-needed rally as a bullion price firming to around $320 an ounce gave a shot in the arm to the ailing sector, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,337.9, up 38.7 points, or 0.53 percent. The All Gold index closed at 947.4, up 42.1 points, or 0.45 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,798.5, up 39.2 points, or 4.65 percent.
